unit_description: This unit applies multiplication and division to problem solving. Students solve equal-group and array problems, use strip models, write equations with unknowns, and handle two-step problems and patterns.
unit_goals: Solve equal-group and array word problems.
Use strip models to represent problems.
Solve two-step multiplication and division problems.
Identify and explain patterns in problems.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students apply multiplication and division to word problems, strip models, equations with unknowns, and two-step problems.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by writing multiplication equations for equal groups and arrays.
lessons.concept: Word problems about equal groups or arrays can be solved with multiplication. If the total and one factor are known, use division to find the missing factor.
lessons.practice: Solve word problems about equal groups and arrays.
lessons.objective: Solve equal-group and array word problems.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by choosing the operation.

questions.prompt: There are 6 boxes with 8 crayons each. How many crayons?
48 crayons are shared equally among 6 boxes. How many in each box?
A shelf has 5 rows of 7 books. How many books?

learn.title: Solve Equal-Group and Array Problems
teaching_points: Find the number of groups and the size of each group.
Divide if the total and one factor are known.

example.prompt: A farmer packs 24 apples into 4 baskets. How many in each basket?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A classroom has 6 tables. Each table has 4 students. How many students?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Solve each equal-group or array word problem.

flashcards.title: Equal Group and Array Words
flashcards.instructions: Review words for equal-group and array problems.

bigIdea.title: Solve Equal-Group and Array Problems
bigIdea.subtitle: Use multiplication and division
bigIdea.intro: Equal-group and array problems use the same three numbers. If you know the groups and size, multiply. If you know the total and one factor, divide.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How are equal-group and array problems related?

ruleCards.description: Multiply groups by size to find the total.
Divide the total by the known factor.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by drawing a strip for a given multiplication fact.
lessons.concept: A strip model is a rectangle divided into equal parts. It can show multiplication, division, and unknown amounts. The total strip represents the product.
lessons.practice: Draw and interpret strip models for multiplication and division problems.
lessons.objective: Use strip models to represent multiplication and division problems.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by matching strips to equations.

questions.prompt: A strip is cut into 5 equal parts. Each part is 6. What is the total?
A total strip is 36. It has 4 equal parts. How long is each part?
A strip has 7 parts of 8. What is the total?

learn.title: Use Strip Models
teaching_points: Draw a strip for the total.
Divide it into equal parts for groups.
Label the unknown with a question mark.

example.prompt: Use a strip model to solve 45 ÷ 9.
example.equation: 45 divided into 9 equal parts is 5 each.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Use a strip model to solve 8 × 7.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Draw a strip model and solve each problem.

bigIdea.title: Use Strip Models
bigIdea.subtitle: Draw a bar to show the problem
bigIdea.intro: A strip model shows the whole and its equal parts. It helps you see whether to multiply or divide and where the unknown is.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How does a strip model help you choose an operation?

ruleCards.description: Multiply the number of parts by the size of each part.
Divide the whole by the number of parts.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by writing equations with a question mark for word problems.
lessons.concept: An unknown number can be shown with a letter or a box. Write an equation that matches the problem, then solve for the unknown.
lessons.practice: Write and solve multiplication and division equations with unknown numbers.
lessons.objective: Write equations with unknown numbers for word problems.

questions.prompt: Write an equation for: 7 times a number is 42.
A number divided by 5 is 6. Write an equation.

learn.title: Write Equations with Unknown Numbers
teaching_points: Use a letter or box for the unknown.
Match the words to an operation.

example.prompt: A number divided by 8 is 7. What is the number?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: 6 times a number is 48. Write an equation and solve.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Write an equation with an unknown and solve each problem.

bigIdea.title: Write Equations with Unknown Numbers
bigIdea.subtitle: Use a letter for what you don't know
bigIdea.intro: When a problem has a number you don't know, use a letter or a box to stand for it. Write an equation that matches the story, then solve.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why is writing an equation helpful for word problems?

ruleCards.description: Use n for the number you need to find.
Use the inverse operation to find the unknown.

lessons.lesson_title: Solve Two-Step Problems and Identify Patterns
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by solving one-step multiplication or division problems quickly.
lessons.concept: Two-step problems need two actions. Look for a pattern after the first step to solve the second step. Use strip models or equations to keep track.
lessons.practice: Solve two-step multiplication and division problems and identify patterns.
lessons.objective: Solve two-step multiplication and division problems and identify patterns.

questions.prompt: A class has 4 groups of 6 students. Then 8 students leave. How many are left?
A box has 24 crayons. 6 students each get 4 crayons. How many crayons are left?

questions.hint: Each number is double the previous.

learn.title: Solve Two-Step Problems and Identify Patterns
teaching_points: Use the result for the second step.

example.prompt: A bakery makes 5 trays of 9 cookies. 12 cookies are sold. How many are left?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A store has 6 boxes of 8 markers. 10 markers are used. How many are left?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Solve each two-step problem and describe any pattern.

flashcards.title: Two-Step and Patterns
flashcards.instructions: Review two-step problem and pattern vocabulary.

bigIdea.title: Solve Two-Step Problems and Identify Patterns
bigIdea.subtitle: Take it one step at a time
bigIdea.intro: Two-step problems have two actions. Solve the first part, then use that answer. Sometimes the numbers make a pattern that helps you check.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How can finding a pattern help you check a two-step problem?

ruleCards.description: Multiply to find the total amount.
Use the total for the second action.

lessons.lesson_title: Unit Evaluation: Multiplication and Division Applications
lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of equal-group/array problems, strip models, equations with unknowns, and two-step problems with patterns.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: equal-group and array problems, strip models, equations with unknowns, and two-step problems with patterns.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about multiplication and division problem solving.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: 7 packs of 8 markers is how many markers?
A strip is 54 divided into 6 equal parts. How long is each part?

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: equal group/array problems + strip models + unknowns + two-step/patterns = applications

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Which equation matches: 5 bags with 7 apples in each?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 18 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 18 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Multiplication and Division Applications
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: equal-group and array problems, strip models, equations with unknowns, and two-step problems with patterns.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about multiplication and division problem solving?

ruleCards.description: Multiplication and division are both about equal groups.
Write an equation to match the problem and solve for the unknown.
